relations.evidence: For more information about the Advanced Self-Recursion Parameter, see [Eventing Functions that Listen to Multiple Collections](eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md#multiple-collection-functions).

notable_absence.finding: Matches the twin's own finding: this worked example introduces no new primitive beyond wildcard bucket-alias bindings, meta.keyspace, and the Advanced Keyspace Accessor family. The same defensive-coding rationale recurs verbatim in the Server code comment: '// Protect against reading from something outside the alias' guards a wildcard-scoped alias from reading/writing outside its intended scope.

cross_component_finding: n/a - see cross_product_finding for this page's real finding.
cross_product_finding: The Server page's own bullet list describes its four required locations as 'keyspaces': 'Requires the following 4 keyspaces in two buckets, `rr100` and source:'. The Capella twin's extraction, by contrast, spoke only of buckets/scopes/collections and used a Capella `scope` concept. This is direct, page-level confirmation of the registry's already-noted split that 'keyspace' is the term the server/ tree uses where the Capella tree says 'collection' (see server:keyspace's registry note). The underlying mechanism - wildcard bucket-alias bindings plus a meta.keyspace guard - is otherwise identical to the Capella twin, code-for-code.
